program_name: Communication Technologies and Multimedia (CTM) — Laurea Magistrale in Tecnologie della Comunicazione e Multimedialità
teaching_language: English — the programme is described on the official University of Brescia pages as a master's degree programme taught in English, and it is listed among the University of Brescia's 'Study programmes taught in English'. NOTE: one search-engine-indexed rendering of the corsi.unibs.it fact box appeared to show 'Language: Italian'; the prevailing official evidence (unibs.it English-taught programmes list + the programme description 'taught in English') supports English. See uncertainty_notes.
campus: Brescia, Italy — Engineering campus of the University of Brescia (Department of Information Engineering / Dipartimento di Ingegneria dell'Informazione, Via Branze area). [uncertain] The exact building/teaching site could not be verified directly because the official pages were unreachable.
english_delivery_scope: fully_english — the whole two-year, 120-ECTS master's degree is delivered in English (it is one of the University of Brescia's fully English-taught master's programmes, alongside e.g. Civil and Environmental Engineering and Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management). [uncertain] Because the corsi.unibs.it page could not be opened directly (Cloudflare human-verification challenge), the 'fully_english' classification rests on the university's English-taught-programmes listing and the official programme description rather than on a directly verified curriculum table listing the language of every single teaching unit.
programme_status: phasing_out_second_year_only — THIS PROGRAMME IS NOT ACCEPTING NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICATIONS FOR 2026/27. The official University of Brescia course pages state that from academic year 2026/27 only the second year of the course will be active, i.e. there is no first-year intake and no new enrolment for incoming students in 2026/27. Only students already enrolled (who completed the first year in 2025/26 or who are transferring/continuing into the second year) can attend. All admission-related fields below (admission_type, academic_requirements, entry test, deadlines, required documents) therefore describe the historical/last-published admission framework and are NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS in 2026/27.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes (historically, and generally for all UNIBS master's degrees) — for candidates holding a foreign qualification, pre-evaluation/pre-assessment by the relevant Commission is compulsory for open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas, in order to verify curricular and personal-preparation requirements. Applications are submitted through the PICA online platform, with a EUR 20 fee paid at the end of the online procedure. For 2026/27 the non-EU pre-assessment round closed on 15 March 2026 (noon, Italian time), with outcomes communicated by email around mid-May 2026. NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS to CTM in 2026/27, because no first-year intake exists for this programme.
entry_test_name: None — there is no named admission test (no TOLC, no CISIA test, no SAT) for this master's degree. Access is 'without restricted access' (open enrolment / accesso libero); instead of a test, the Programme Council (Consiglio di Corso di Studio) verifies (a) fulfilment of curricular requirements expressed as minimum ECTS in specified SSDs and (b) the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation. NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS in 2026/27.
admission_type: open access (accesso libero / 'course without restricted access'), subject to verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation — NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW APPLICANTS in 2026/27, since only the second year of the course is active from A.Y. 2026/27.
academic_requirements: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — recorded here as the last published framework.] Applicants must hold an Italian three-year Bachelor's degree (laurea triennale) or a university diploma, or another foreign qualification recognised as suitable. Applicants holding a degree under DM 270/04 (or the previous DM 509/99) must have earned a minimum number of ECTS/CFU in specific scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) as detailed in the Programme Regulations (Regolamento Didattico del Corso di Studio); the reference/benchmark curriculum is the Bachelor's Degree in Electronic and Telecommunications Engineering (class L-8, Information Engineering) of the University of Brescia. Admission is decided by the Programme Council, which assesses fulfilment of the curricular requirements, evaluates the academic record, and verifies the adequacy of personal preparation according to the procedures set in the Programme Regulations; the candidate is admitted only if both evaluations are positive. [uncertain] The exact SSD codes and the exact per-SSD minimum CFU thresholds could not be extracted because the official Regolamento Didattico page/PDF could not be opened directly.
language_requirements: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — last published framework.] The University of Brescia's general rule is that all master's degree programmes (Corsi di Laurea magistrale) in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas require English language proficiency at least at level B1 CEFR. Instead of an official English certificate, study programmes may accept candidates who completed their previous educational pathway in English or who passed English language examinations during their academic studies; the university's CLA (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) language certificate is also used as evidence. [uncertain] Because Communication Technologies and Multimedia is fully English-taught, a higher effective level (commonly B2 CEFR) is normally expected/required by the programme itself, and the STAR/LMINT scholarship calls for English-taught master's degrees set their own English evidence requirements — but the programme-specific minimum level and the exact list of accepted certificates (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge scores) could not be verified directly.
application_deadline_eu: Not applicable for 2026/27 — no first-year intake for this programme. [uncertain] For UNIBS master's degrees in general, EU and EU-equivalent citizens holding a foreign qualification apply for pre-assessment in dedicated rounds published each year (a previous round ran 30 June – 21 July at noon Italian time), and enrolment/matriculation deadlines for master's degrees vary by programme and typically run from summer through December of the academic year. The specific EU deadline that would have applied to CTM could not be verified directly.
application_deadline_non_eu: Not applicable for 2026/27 — no first-year intake for this programme. For reference, the general UNIBS pre-assessment procedure for non-EU candidates with foreign qualifications aiming to enrol in Italian- or English-taught master's degrees in 2026/2027 was open until 15 March 2026 (noon, Italian time) via the PICA online platform, with outcomes notified by email around mid-May 2026; this is the university-level pre-assessment/scholarship deadline and is SEPARATE from the later Universitaly pre-enrolment and student-visa procedure handled through Italian diplomatic missions.
required_documents: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27 — last published framework.] For the PICA pre-assessment / pre-evaluation application for master's degrees: bachelor's degree certificate (or certificate of expected graduation), full academic transcript with list of examinations and ECTS/credits, evidence of English language proficiency (certificate or equivalent evidence), copy of passport/identity document, curriculum vitae, and payment of the EUR 20 pre-assessment fee. For final enrolment, foreign qualifications must be accompanied by the standard Italian documentation for foreign degrees — Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic mission, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification, together with legalised/translated diploma and transcript; non-EU candidates residing abroad additionally complete Universitaly pre-enrolment for the study visa. [uncertain] The exact document checklist specific to this programme could not be verified directly.
entry_exam_or_test: [NOT APPLICABLE FOR NEW FIRST-YEAR APPLICANTS 2026/27.] No written entrance examination and no standardised admission test. Admission is based on a documentary assessment: the Programme Council verifies (1) the curricular requirements (minimum ECTS in the SSDs listed in the Programme Regulations, benchmarked on the UNIBS L-8 Electronic and Telecommunications Engineering bachelor) and (2) the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation, using procedures set in the Programme Regulations and taking account of the results obtained in the degree used for admission. [uncertain] Whether an interview (colloquio) is used in practice when personal preparation is not automatically satisfied could not be verified directly; UNIBS programme regulations commonly provide for an interview in that case.

uncertainty_notes:
1) DIRECT PAGE ACCESS FAILED — MANDATORY CAVEAT: neither https://corsi.unibs.it/en/communicationtechnologiesandmultimedia nor https://corsi.unibs.it/en/communicationtechnologiesandmultimedia/enrolling could be retrieved directly. Automated fetching returned HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for corsi.unibs.it and HTTP 403 Forbidden for www.unibs.it / en.unibs.it; opening the site in a browser produced a Cloudflare 'Human Verification' challenge page with no readable content. Completing or bypassing that bot-detection challenge is not permitted, so ALL content in this record was compiled from search-engine indexed snippets and cached summaries of the official pages rather than from directly verified live pages. Quotes reproduced in source_quotes are therefore indexed renderings and may differ in exact wording, and any figures could be from an earlier crawl of the page.

2) ENROLMENT STATUS FOR 2026/27 — EXPLICIT ANSWER: this programme is NOT accepting new first-year applications for academic year 2026/27. The official course page states that from A.Y. 2026/27 only the second year of the course will be active. In practice this means the programme is being phased out / restructured, the first-year cohort has been discontinued, and all admission requirements, entry procedures, and deadlines recorded above apply only historically and are 'not applicable for new applicants'. Prospective students should treat this programme as closed to new entrants for 2026/27. [uncertain] The reason for the phase-out (closure vs. replacement by a successor degree, e.g. a reorganised LM-27 or a merged Information Engineering master) could not be verified, and no official statement about a replacement programme was found in indexed content.

3) TEACHING LANGUAGE CONFLICT: the official programme description on www.unibs.it explicitly says the programme is 'taught in English', and CTM appears on the University of Brescia's 'Study programmes taught in English' page (https://www.unibs.it/en/english-study-programmes) together with Civil and Environmental Engineering and Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management. However, one search-engine-indexed rendering of the corsi.unibs.it fact box reported 'Language: Italian'. This is most likely an artefact of the Italian-language version of the fact box being indexed, or of an outdated crawl, but it could not be resolved because the live page is unreachable. teaching_language and english_delivery_scope are therefore recorded as English / fully_english with this conflict flagged; a directly verified check of the course-unit list (which language each teaching unit is delivered in) was not possible.

4) DEGREE CLASS: LM-27 (Telecommunications Engineering) is well supported by indexed content, including the career-outcomes statement referring to LM-27/LM-26 for public-administration engineering competitions. Considered reliable.

5) FIELDS THAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED IN DETAIL: exact SSD codes and per-SSD minimum CFU thresholds in the curricular requirements; the programme-specific English level (B1 general university rule vs. B2 commonly expected for a fully English-taught degree) and the exact accepted certificates; whether a personal-preparation interview is used; the exact document checklist; the precise EU application/enrolment deadline; and current tuition amounts. These are marked [uncertain] in their respective fields.

6) DEADLINES RECORDED ARE UNIVERSITY-LEVEL, NOT PROGRAMME-LEVEL: the 15 March 2026 (noon Italian time) date is the general UNIBS non-EU pre-assessment / STAR + LMINT scholarship deadline for master's degrees, not a CTM-specific call, and since CTM has no 2026/27 first-year intake it does not apply to this programme at all. It must not be confused with the Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa timeline, which is a separate national procedure.

7) SOURCE POLICY: only unibs.it / corsi.unibs.it URLs were used as sources, as required. Third-party aggregators (Mastersportal, educations.com, AlmaLaurea) appeared in search results but were deliberately NOT used as evidence.
